name: 86. DeepSeek max_tokens cap dropped on OpenAI-compatible wire (#5606) (deepseek-max-tokens-cap)
description: Issue #5606: Bifrost collapses an inbound max_tokens into ChatParameters.MaxCompletionTokens at the transport, then the OpenAI egress converter emits it as max_completion_tokens. DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions reads only the legacy max_tokens spelling and ignores unknown fields silently, so the output cap was dropped with no error at any layer - reported at 266-289x the requested cap (4629 tokens returned for max_tokens:16) with finish_reason 'stop'. The fix renames the field back to max_tokens in the DeepSeek case of ToOpenAIChatRequest, alongside the existing OpenCode/Ollama/Mistral cases. These rows pin the cap as observable behaviour rather than as a wire-field name: a honored cap truncates an essay prompt at 16 tokens and reports finish_reason 'length'. Pre-fix all three fail with finish_reason 'stop' and thousands of completion tokens. max_tokens is exactly 16 so Bifrost's MinMaxCompletionTokens clamp is a no-op and cannot mask the result. Content is deliberately not asserted: DeepSeek thinks by default, so a 16-token cap can legitimately truncate inside reasoning and leave content empty.

exec: pm.test('deepseek native route max_tokens: max_tokens cap honored (finish_reason=length) - #5606', function () {

pm.expect(j.choices[0].finish_reason, 'max_tokens:16 was not honored - DeepSeek reads the legacy max_tokens field and silently ignores max_completion_tokens, so a renamed field lets generation run uncapped: ' + pm.response.text()).to.eql('length');
pm.test('deepseek native route max_tokens: completion_tokens stays near the cap - #5606', function () {
pm.expect(u.completion_tokens, 'requested max_tokens:16 but got ' + u.completion_tokens + ' completion tokens - the output cap was dropped in translation (#5606)').to.be.at.most(64);

body.raw: {"model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a detailed 800 word essay about the history of the Eiffel Tower, covering its design, construction and reception."}],"max_tokens":16}
